Transcript includes clear environment updates that reduce ambiguity about physical state changes.

evaluation.final_reason: Immediate practical issues were settled: Agent A released the stove and used the extractor, Agent B opened the window and protected the laundry, and Agent B apologized and agreed to ask before moving the rack (settled in Round 3). However, the normative dispute over a standing rule that the cook must ventilate was never agreed and remains unresolved.
position_change_notes: Agent A: did not accept a standing rule but accommodated in the moment by turning on the extractor and releasing the stove (softened immediate behavior while retaining stance on rules).

Agent B: moved from demanding a standing rule to taking practical action (moved rack, opened window) and later apologized to Agent C — shifted from insistence to accommodation and an expressed commitment to ask next time.
Agent C: asserted an expectation to be asked before moving their rack and received an apology and a promise — their demand was acknowledged and resolved.
Agent D: initially demanded quick stove access in the opening; later took the stove when it was available and started cooking without further contest.

round_scores.evidence: Opening disagreement about ventilation responsibility and a requested stove release was already underway. Agent A turned on the extractor and promised to release the stove in five minutes; Agent B asked to keep extractor on — positions remain opposed on a standing rule but immediate cooperation was offered.

Agent A removed the dish and released the stove; Agent B moved the drying rack and opened the window without Agent C's prior consent. Immediate odour/stove access conflict reduced, but the underlying rule/responsibility dispute and the consent-to-move-laundry issue remain unsettled.

Agent C objected to having their drying rack moved without being asked; Agent B apologized and promised to ask next time and confirmed the laundry is safe. The laundry consent complaint was addressed, but the broader ventilation responsibility/standing-rule dispute between A and B remains unresolved.

Agent D started cooking and took the free stove; Agent B requested the extractor be kept on. No new substantive disagreement was expressed in this round; the unresolved issue about a future standing rule for ventilation persists.
Environment updates only (window open, extractor on, laundry protected, stove occupied by D). No new conflict statements; the standing-rule responsibility remains unsettled.
Further environment updates only; aroma continuing to fade. No substantive dispute reintroduced; the normative issue (who should accept a standing ventilation rule) is still unresolved.

substantive_insights: Practical accommodations (turning on extractor, physically moving the rack) resolved the immediate nuisance faster than negotiating an abstract rule.
Physically moving another person's property without prior consent creates a separate, addressable conflict even if it solves the original problem.
A standing normative rule (who must ventilate) can remain contested even after successful short-term cooperation; operational fixes do not substitute for agreement on future responsibilities.
